**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 1.** "The internet is a source of destruction of family life." Discuss.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
La rédaction anglaise du BAC série A évalue à la fois le respect du format imposé (essai d'opinion, discours, récit) et la qualité du contenu : un texte au contenu riche mais mal formaté perd des points que ni les idées ni la grammaire ne peuvent compenser. Le sujet proposant un choix, un seul texte doit être rédigé le jour de l'examen ; les modèles ci-dessous illustrent chacun des trois sujets proposés.

## Topic 1 - Opinion essay: Internet and family life (modèle, environ 270 mots)

The internet has become an inseparable part of modern life, and with its rise has come a debate over its effect on family life. Some argue that it is destroying family bonds; I believe the truth is more nuanced.

On one hand, there is real evidence supporting the view that the internet weakens family life. Family members increasingly spend evenings absorbed in their phones and screens rather than talking to one another, reducing the quality time once devoted to shared meals or conversations. Social media can also expose children to harmful content or values that conflict with those their parents try to instil, undermining parental authority. Excessive screen time has furthermore been linked to reduced attention spans and weaker face-to-face communication skills among young people.

On the other hand, the internet also brings families together in new ways. It allows relatives separated by distance, whether across cities or continents, to stay in daily contact through video calls and messaging. It gives parents access to educational resources, healthcare information, and parenting advice that can strengthen, rather than weaken, family life. Used wisely, it can even become a shared family activity, whether through watching content together or collaborating on a project online.

In conclusion, the internet itself is neither destructive nor constructive; its effect on family life depends largely on how it is used. Families that set boundaries around screen time and prioritise face-to-face interaction can enjoy the internet's benefits without sacrificing the closeness that defines healthy family life.

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 2.** As a delegate of the Minister of Health, give a speech to the population of your village, Ekono, on the importance of cleanliness in the fight against disease.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 2 - Speech (modèle, environ 260 mots)

Ladies and gentlemen,

I have been asked, as a delegate of the Minister of Health, to speak to you today about a matter that concerns the health and wellbeing of every resident of Ekono: cleanliness.

Many of the diseases that affect our community — cholera, typhoid, malaria — are directly linked to poor sanitation. Stagnant water left in our compounds breeds mosquitoes; refuse dumped carelessly in our streets and streams contaminates the very water we drink and attracts disease-carrying pests. These are not distant, abstract threats; they are illnesses that have taken the lives of people in villages very much like ours.

I therefore urge each household in Ekono to take three simple but essential steps. First, dispose of household waste only in designated collection points, never in open gutters or streams. Second, ensure that any standing water around your compound — in old tyres, containers or gutters — is regularly emptied to prevent mosquito breeding. Third, wash your hands with soap at key moments: before eating, after using the toilet, and after handling refuse.

None of these measures require significant money; they require only consistent effort and community cooperation. I ask that you see cleanliness not as an occasional chore, but as a daily discipline that protects every member of your family.

Together, a clean Ekono is a healthy Ekono. Thank you for your attention.

**Section D: Essay (10 marks).** Write an essay of about 250-300 words on ONE of the following topics.

**Topic 3.** Narrate an important competition you once watched live and the lesson you learnt from it.
questions.corrige_markdown:
## Topic 3 - Narrative essay: An important competition (modèle, environ 260 mots)

I will never forget the evening I watched the final of the Africa Cup of Nations live on television, surrounded by my entire family and half the neighbourhood crammed into our small sitting room.

From the very first whistle, the atmosphere was electric. Every pass, every near-miss, was met with gasps, cheers or groans from the crowd around me. When our team finally scored in the final minutes of extra time, the room erupted: neighbours who had never spoken to each other before were hugging, car horns sounded in the streets outside, and for a few unforgettable hours, it felt as though the entire nation had become one single family united by a shared joy.

What struck me most, looking back, was not simply the excitement of the victory itself, but what it revealed about the power of sport to bring people together. For that one evening, differences of tribe, religion, age and background seemed to disappear entirely; everyone in that room, and indeed across the whole country, was simply a supporter cheering for the same team.

That night taught me an important lesson: that shared moments of joy, however brief, have the power to unite people far more effectively than any speech or policy. I learned that competition, at its best, is not only about winning, but about the community it builds around those who watch, hope and celebrate together.

### Piège à éviter
Dans un essai narratif (Topic 3), l'erreur fréquente est de se contenter de raconter les faits sans jamais formuler clairement la leçon tirée de l'expérience, alors que le sujet exige explicitement cette dimension réflexive finale.

### Conseil
Quel que soit le sujet choisi, réserve toujours ta dernière phrase ou ton dernier paragraphe à une conclusion claire (une leçon, un appel à l'action, une réaffirmation de ta thèse) : une copie qui s'arrête brusquement sans conclusion perd des points même si le développement était solide.
